title: Prefill probe pipeline accelerator for low-latency prompt preprocessing
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Reduce prefill-side overhead by introducing a lightweight 'probe' pass that rapidly classifies incoming prompts and routes them through specialized fast-paths (ascii/binary, short-prefix, cached-session) and selects kernel and attention strategies before full tokenization. Goal is to cut median prefill CPU time and wall-clock latency for common short prompts while preserving correctness and cache hit behaviour.
motivation: Current prefill pipeline spends disproportionate time in a generic normalization + tokenization path for small, high-QPS prompts (e.g., chat messages, system prompts). This increases tail latency and reduces opportunities for KV cache prewarm. A fast probe can cheaply decide whether to short-circuit heavy normalization, reuse cached encodings, or pick a specialized kernel layout that reduces transient memory copies.
success_metrics:
1) Median prefill wall time for prompts <128 chars reduced by 35% (baseline: 3.2ms)
2) 95th percentile prefill latency for low-seq requests reduced by 25%
3) End-to-end decode latency degradation <2% for long prompts
4) No regressions in tokenization correctness (pass fuzz corpus)
5) Cache hit rate for session prefix prefill increases by >=8%
design_notes:
- Add a lightweight Probe stage at RPC ingress that uses a compact heuristic vector: is_ascii, heuristic_token_count_estimate, special_char_ratio, session_prefill_hint.
- Probe output: tag (FAST_ASCII | SHORT_PREFIX | SESSION_CACHED | GENERIC), and recommended kernel profile id.
- Fast paths: ASCII fast lane (byte-level tokenizer + direct prefill cache lookup), Short-prefix inline lexer (vectorized), Session-cached replay (emit cached token ids and kv snapshot), Generic fallback.
- Kernel selection: map probe tags to precompiled kernel variants that are optimized for short sequences (reduced kernel launch params, fused normalization+tokenize kernels).
- Safety: probe must be deterministic and have a checksum fallback — if probe and tokenizer disagree on token boundaries, fallback to GENERIC path and emit telemetry.
- Observability: expose probe decisions and per-path latencies in Console; add a probe-decision attribute to trace spans.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Implement probe library in C++ runtime (2w) with unit tests and deterministic checksum. Phase 2: Integrate probe at RPC ingress and wire kernel-selection hooks (2w). Phase 3: Implement ASCII fast lane and session cache lookup (2w). Phase 4: End-to-end benchmarks, correctness fuzzing, and canary rollout (1w).
Notes: keep probe fully opt-in behind feature flag 'probe_prefill_v1' and a tenant whitelist for Dedicated/Private customers during canary.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal perf lab run to validate microbenchmarks and memory impact. 2) Canary on staging with 10% of traffic where feature flag is enabled. 3) Monitor metrics (prefill latency, cache hit rate, tokenization mismatch rate) for 48h. 4) Expand canary to 30%, then 100% assuming no regressions. 5) Post-rollout 7-day evaluation and revert if mismatch rate >0.01%.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: Probe misclassification causes tokenization mismatches. Mitigation: Deterministic checksum compare between probe-tokenized and canonical tokenizer on a sampled subset (1/1000 requests). If mismatch observed, auto-disable probe for that tenant and log detailed diff.
- Risk: Memory pressure from additional kernel variants. Mitigation: limit compiled kernels to top-3 variants and evict others dynamically; track resident set size in lab runs.
- Risk: Unintended latency regressions for long prompts. Mitigation: probe explicitly tags only short prompts (<=512 bytes) and defaults to GENERIC otherwise.
